Description: The Roche/454 GS (Genome Sequencer) is a high-throughput pyrosequencing instrument developed by 454 Life Sciences, one of the first commercially available next-generation DNA sequencing platforms.
The 454 GS 20 is a high-throughput pyrosequencing instrument developed by 454 Life Sciences, the first commercially released model in the GS sequencer line.

The 454 GS FLX is a next-generation pyrosequencing instrument developed by 454 Life Sciences (later Roche) that uses emulsion PCR-amplified beads and sequencing-by-synthesis with bioluminescent detection.
The 454 GS FLX Titanium sequencer is a GS high-throughput sequencing machine developed by 454 Life Sciences, an upgraded version of the GS FLX offering increased read length and throughput.
The 454 GS FLX+ is an upgraded version of the 454 GS FLX Titanium pyrosequencing instrument from 454 Life Sciences (Roche), offering extended read lengths of up to approximately 1,000 bp.
The 454 GS Junior is a benchtop high-throughput pyrosequencing machine developed by 454 Life Sciences, a smaller-scale version of the GS FLX system.
An Applied Biosystems sequencing instrument that uses a single-capillary electrophoresis system to perform automated Sanger sequencing and fragment analysis.
An Applied Biosystems sequencing instrument that performs capillary electrophoresis-based Sanger sequencing using 4 capillaries; successor to the AB PRISM 310.
An Applied Biosystems sequencing instrument that performs capillary electrophoresis-based Sanger sequencing using 16 capillaries; successor to the AB PRISM 310.
An Applied Biosystems sequencing instrument that performs capillary electrophoresis-based Sanger sequencing using 8 capillaries and can run 96-well plates; successor to the 3130 series.
An Applied Biosystems sequencing instrument that performs capillary electrophoresis-based Sanger sequencing using 24 capillaries and can run 384-well plates; successor to the 3130 series.
An Applied Biosystems sequencing instrument that uses a 48-capillary array electrophoresis system for Sanger sequencing; successor to the 3500 series.
An Applied Biosystems sequencing instrument that uses a 96-capillary array electrophoresis system for Sanger sequencing; successor to the 3500 series.

A proprietary next-generation DNA sequencing system from Applied Biosystems that utilizes DNA ligase. DNA fragments attached to beads are clonally amplified and ligated to fluorescently labeled "interrogation probes". Ligation frees the fluor, which is detected and identifies the specific probe. The marker of the attached probe is then removed and a 5'-phosphate group is regenerated. Multiple cycles of ligation, detection, and cleavage are performed.

The BGISEQ-500 is a model type of the BGISEQ sequencing library platform.

A DNA sequencer manufactured by Oxford Nanopore Technologies that can run and analyze up to five individual flow cells, producing up to 150 Gb of data per run, using real-time nanopore sequencing.
The HeliScope is a DNA sequencer manufactured by Helicos BioSciences that performs single-molecule sequencing of unamplified DNA templates using reversible-terminator chemistry.
A DNA sequencer manufactured by Solexa (later acquired by Illumina) as one of its first sequencer lines, launched in 2006, capable of sequencing 1 gigabase (Gb) of data in a single run.
A DNA sequencer developed by Illumina; an upgraded version of the original Genome Analyzer supporting single- or paired-end sequencing by synthesis.

An upgraded Illumina Genome Analyzer II model that supports sequencing of single, long, or short-insert paired-end clone libraries using sequencing-by-synthesis technology; one of the most widely adopted early next-generation sequencing platforms.

A DNA sequencer manufactured by Illumina using sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry, containing a HiScan Reader for sequencing and microarray-based analyses as well as an SQ Module supporting microfluidics.
The Illumina HiSeq 1000 is a sequencing machine developed by Illumina with a single flow cell and a throughput of up to 35 Gb per day.
The Illumina HiSeq 1500 is a sequencing machine developed by Illumina, with a single flow cell and dual surface imaging offering high-output and rapid-run modes.
The Illumina HiSeq 2000 is a sequencing machine developed by Illumina with two flow cells and a throughput of up to 55 Gb per day, optimized for multi-sample sequencing.
The Illumina HiSeq 2500 is a sequencing machine developed by Illumina with two flow cells and a throughput of up to 160 Gb per day, supporting both high-output batch runs and rapid-run modes.
The Illumina HiSeq 3000 is a high-throughput sequencing machine developed by Illumina with a single flow cell and a throughput of more than 200 Gb per day.
The Illumina HiSeq 4000 is a high-throughput sequencing machine developed by Illumina with two flow cells and a throughput of more than 400 Gb per day.

A DNA sequencer manufactured by Illumina using sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry, consisting of a set of five HiSeq X ultra-high-throughput sequencing systems configured for population-scale whole-genome sequencing.
A DNA sequencer manufactured by Illumina consisting of a set of ten HiSeq X ultra-high-throughput sequencing systems configured for population-scale whole-genome sequencing.
The Illumina iSeq 100 is a model type of the Illumina sequencing library platform.
A benchtop DNA sequencer manufactured by Illumina using sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry, with an output capacity of approximately 1.65-7.5 Gb per run.
The Illumina MiSeq is a high-throughput sequencing machine developed by Illumina; primary applications include small whole-genome sequencing, targeted gene sequencing, and 16S metagenomic sequencing.
A benchtop DNA sequencer manufactured by Illumina using sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry; the NextSeq series succeeded the HiSeq/MiSeq lines with high throughput in a compact benchtop format.

This name does not correspond to a standard commercially released Illumina platform; it appears to conflate the Illumina NextSeq (500/550) benchtop sequencer series with the HiSeq 2500. The Illumina NextSeq 500 is a benchtop high-throughput sequencing machine developed by Illumina using sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry.

The Illumina NextSeq 550 is a benchtop high-throughput sequencing machine developed by Illumina; primary applications include exome sequencing, targeted gene sequencing, whole-transcriptome sequencing, and cytogenomic arrays.
A DNA sequencer manufactured by Illumina using sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry with an output capacity of up to 6 Tb and 20 billion reads in dual flow-cell mode.

The Illumina NovaSeq 6000 is a high-throughput sequencing machine developed by Illumina, with two flow cells and an output of up to 6000 Gb using patterned flow-cell sequencing-by-synthesis technology.
The Illumina NovaSeq X Plus is a high-throughput sequencing machine developed by Illumina with a dual flow-cell configuration and an output of up to 16 Tb per run using XLEAP-SBS chemistry.
A DNA sequencer manufactured by Ion Torrent (Thermo Fisher) that utilizes ion semiconductor sequencing and has an output capacity of 300 Mb to 1 Gb.
A DNA sequencer manufactured by Ion Torrent (Thermo Fisher) that utilizes ion semiconductor sequencing and has an output capacity of up to 15 Gb.
A DNA sequencer manufactured by Ion Torrent (Thermo Fisher) that utilizes ion semiconductor sequencing and requires only a small amount of input material.

A DNA sequencer manufactured by Ion Torrent (Thermo Fisher) that utilizes ion semiconductor sequencing, requiring only a small amount of input material while producing data faster than the standard S5 model.
